title: Euler's Number (e)
subtitle: Transcendental constant · Analysis
summary: Base of the natural logarithm. The unique number where d/dx eˣ = eˣ.
detail:
\[ e = \lim_{n\to\infty}\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)^n = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n!} = 2.71828\ldots \]

Transcendental (Hermite, 1873). The exponential function \(e^x\) is its own derivative. The natural logarithm \(\ln x\) is its inverse. Appears in compound interest, normal distributions, Fourier analysis, and complex analysis via Euler's formula \(e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta\).
